references.text: God promises to keep his covenant with Israel if they obey his commands, which reflects the conditions in Deuteronomy 7:12.
Describes the blessings that follow from obedience to God's commands and keeping his covenant.
Parallel text promising blessings for obedience to God's commands and statutes.
God confirms the covenant he swore to the fathers, a central theme in Deuteronomy 7:12.
God's covenant with Abraham, which he swore to the fathers, mentioned in Deuteronomy 7:12.
God affirms the oath he swore to Abraham, which is the foundation of the covenant mentioned in Deuteronomy 7:12.
God's mercy and covenant are for those who keep his commands, reflecting the theme of obedience and God's faithfulness.
God remembers his covenant forever, the one he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Nehemiah refers to God as one who keeps his covenant and shows mercy to those who love him and keep his commands.
Daniel confesses that God keeps his covenant and shows mercy to those who love him and keep his commands.
John emphasizes that we know God by keeping his commands, which reflects the conditions of the covenant.
Refers to God's oath to Abraham and his unchangeable promise, which is the foundation of the covenant.
